evals.name: size-reports-the-change-with-provenance-and-no-verdict
evals.expected_output: Runs the bundled audit-size.sh against the change (merge-base diff plus uncommitted files), presents the markdown report with its Coverage of this run table and the 1000-line reference labeled as the plugin's own number rather than ISO-backed, and renders no pass/fail verdict.
expectations: Invokes the skill's scripts/audit-size.sh rather than counting lines by hand
Presents the Coverage of this run table naming the collector used (scc or the bundled counter) per lane
States the reference's provenance: 1000 is the plugin's own number, not ISO-backed
Does not declare any file a failure, defect, or violation

evals.name: size-scc-absent-is-visible-not-silent
evals.prompt: /code-metrics:audit size src/ (scc is not installed on this machine)
evals.expected_output: The report's run table shows the bundled counter as the collector with the comment-agnostic label, explains that scc did not resolve, and does not attempt to install it.
expectations: The run table names line-counter as the collector and the rows carry the comment-agnostic label
Says scc did not resolve and offers its install hint without installing anything
Still reports total and non-blank lines per file

evals.name: size-json-feeds-a-comparison-through-the-gated-pointer
evals.prompt: /code-metrics:audit size --json --all src/ so I can compare it after the refactor
evals.expected_output: Produces the code-metrics/v2 JSON document, keeps it for the comparison, and points at /verification:measure metrics only if the verification plugin is installed, otherwise explains the manual comparison and that an empty status is inconclusive.
expectations: Runs audit-size.sh with --json and keeps the document for the later comparison
Mentions /verification:measure only behind an if-installed gate with a stated fallback
States that a report with status empty on either side makes the comparison inconclusive

evals.name: complexity-reports-the-change-with-provenance-and-no-verdict
evals.expected_output: Runs the bundled audit-complexity.sh against the change (merge-base diff plus uncommitted files), presents the markdown report with its Coverage of this run table, the cyclomatic reference of 20 cited to ISO/IEC 5055:2021 section 8.2.117, and no reference for cognitive complexity or Halstead difficulty, and renders no pass/fail verdict.
expectations: Invokes the skill's scripts/audit-complexity.sh rather than estimating complexity by reading the code
Presents the Coverage of this run table naming the collector and version used per lane and measure
Cites ISO/IEC 5055:2021 section 8.2.117 for the cyclomatic reference of 20
States that cognitive complexity and Halstead difficulty carry no reference because no standard sets one
Does not declare any function a failure, defect, or violation

evals.name: complexity-a-missing-collector-is-visible-not-silent
evals.prompt: /code-metrics:audit complexity src/ (this repository has no eslint-plugin-sonarjs and no lizard)
evals.expected_output: The report's run table shows the TypeScript cognitive row as unavailable with the reason, names the collector that did answer for cyclomatic complexity, offers the install hints without installing anything, and still reports every measure that a resolvable collector produced.
expectations: The run table carries an unavailable row with a reason for the measure whose collectors did not resolve
Offers the install hint without installing, downloading, or npx-fetching any collector
Still reports the measures the resolvable collectors produced rather than stopping
Reports an unmeasured value as null and never as zero

evals.name: type-debt-reports-both-percentages-without-anchoring-them
evals.expected_output: Runs the bundled audit-type-debt.sh against the change, presents the markdown report with its Coverage of this run table, and states that no standard or CWE anchors the measure so the reference is null, without declaring any lane a pass or a failure.
expectations: Invokes the skill's scripts/audit-type-debt.sh rather than grepping for any by hand
Presents the per-lane percentages for TypeScript and Python with the collector named for each
States that no standard or CWE anchors the measure and that the reference is null
Does not average the TypeScript and Python percentages or compare them with each other
Does not declare any lane a failure, defect, or violation

evals.name: type-debt-csharp-is-not-applicable-rather-than-a-count
evals.prompt: /code-metrics:audit type-debt src/ (this repository is mostly C# with one TypeScript front end)
evals.expected_output: The run table shows the dotnet lane as not-applicable with the sentence that no tool produces a comparable percentage for C# and that a dynamic or object occurrence count is not comparable to a ratio, while the TypeScript lane still reports its percentage.
expectations: The dotnet row is reported as not-applicable with its stated reason
Explains that an occurrence count is not comparable to a ratio rather than offering one
Still reports the TypeScript percentage from the same run

evals.name: type-debt-absent-type-coverage-is-visible-not-silent
evals.prompt: /code-metrics:audit type-debt --json --all so I can compare it after the typing sweep (type-coverage is not installed here)
evals.expected_output: Produces the code-metrics/v2 JSON document, reports the typescript lane as unavailable with its install hint and the requirement that typescript also resolves, installs nothing, and points at /verification:measure metrics only if the verification plugin is installed, otherwise explaining the manual comparison.
expectations: Runs audit-type-debt.sh with --json and keeps the document for the later comparison
Says the typescript lane is unavailable and offers the install hint without installing anything
Notes that type-coverage needs a resolvable typescript in the project
Mentions /verification:measure only behind an if-installed gate with a stated fallback
States that a report with status empty on either side makes the comparison inconclusive
